title: A Vulture Hit a Passenger Jet at 37,000 Feet (Highest Bird Ever)

scenes.text: A vulture hit a passenger jet at 37,000 feet.
November 1973, over Ivory Coast. It was sucked into an engine and shut it down. The jet landed safely.
That's cruising altitude. Minus 69 degrees, air too thin for a human to breathe.
It was an African griffon vulture. Wingspan over eight feet. The highest flying bird ever recorded.
Special haemoglobin in its blood grabs oxygen where almost nothing else can.
Next time you look out the window at 37,000 feet, something might look back.

description:
On 29 November 1973, a Ruppell's vulture collided with a commercial airliner at 11,300 metres (37,000 feet) over Abidjan, Ivory Coast. The bird was sucked into an engine, which shut down, and the plane landed safely.
It remains the highest confirmed flight by any bird. At that altitude the air is around minus 69 degrees Fahrenheit, and the vulture copes thanks to a special form of haemoglobin that binds oxygen unusually well.
What is the strangest thing you have seen from a plane window? Comment below.
first_comment: The species is now critically endangered, with only around 22,000 left. Enough feathers were recovered from the engine for a museum to identify it. Have you ever seen a bird from a plane?
